thread:
Maya S.: Heads-up — Customer ACME-Analytics just escalated: their invoice shows 720 reserved GPU hours for Feb but their dashboard reserved-pool shows 480 hours and token burn looks low. They think we're double-charging burst capacity. Can billing/infra triage? :warning:
Jordan B.: Thanks — can you paste the invoice line items and the dashboard snapshot? also need the customer pool id and their reserved contract id.
Maya S.: Pool id: pool-2234, contract: DED-ACME-2025-1. Invoice excerpt: `line_item: reserved_capacity_hours = 720, unit_price = $4/hr`. Dashboard export (CSV) shows `reserved_hours_used = 480`, `burst_hours = 118`, `dedicated_pool_gpu_hours = 598` (weird).
Jordan B.: Hmm. invoice 720 vs dashboard reserved 480. But dashboard dedicated_pool_gpu_hours 598 is suspicious — maybe attribution mixed reserved+burst. Adding Ashok.
Ashok R.: I can look at metering. Two quick hypotheses: 1) attribution tag lost on some runner tasks (so burst got attributed to reserved) 2) a reconciliation job reclassed burst hours as reserved during finalization. Will pull raw meter logs.
billing-bot: Metering export for pool-2234 (raw_summary): {"reserved_hours_reported":"480","burst_hours_reported":"118","total_gpu_hours_raw":"598","invoice_applied_reserved_hours":"720"} — reconciliation job run at 2026-02-28T23:50Z.
Maya S.: Reconciliation job? Jordan, did finance run any end-of-month adjustments?
Jordan B.: Finance triggered the finalize-reconciliation job (ID recon-20260228-17) to close out multi-region accounting. It should never inflate reserved hours though. I'll pull the job logs.
Ashok R.: I'm running a quick query against metering events: ```sql
SELECT timestamp, job_id, attribution_key, gpu_hours, meter_type
FROM metering.events
WHERE pool_id = 'pool-2234' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28';
```
Ashok R.: Early findings: ~242 hours (in a single contiguous window on 2026-02-27 03:00-13:00 UTC) have NULL attribution_key and were tagged as "reserved" by the finalizer because it defaulted missing attribution => reserved. Those were actually burst routing to shared pool during an autoscaler bounce.
Sam C.: That 242 hours = 480 vs 720 gap? 480 + 242 = 722, matches invoice. So this explains it. Sam (CS): Customer saw their dashboard pull earlier that didn't include finalizer adjustments. They were confused.
Maya S.: Great catch. Can we confirm root cause of NULL attribution? What broke earlier that caused the attribution tags to drop?
Ashok R.: Tracing the request path: during the autoscaler restart, the request router (route-agent v1.14) retried against fallback backend without propagating X-Pool-Attribution header when the connection was proxied through the new instance. There's a known flaky edge-case that lost headers on connection reuse. I've got the repro steps.
Ashok R.: Repro (local): ```bash
# emulate router bounce
docker run --rm router:v1.14 /bin/sh -c "curl -H 'X-Pool-Attribution: pool-2234' http://internal-runner/compute && restart-router && curl http://internal-runner/compute"
# observe second request missing header
```
Jordan B.: So finalizer treats missing attribution as reserved by default. That's the reconciliation bug. We need three actions: 1) scope a hotfix to finalizer to not default to reserved, 2) patch router to preserve headers on retry, 3) credit the customer for the mis-attributed 242 hours. Agree?
Maya S.: Agree. Customer wants an explanation and provisional credit while we investigate. I'll draft the reply once we have numbers & ticket.
Ashok R.: I'll open infra ticket and attach detailed logs (infra-3245). Patch plan: route-agent v1.14.1 to fix header propagation, will rollout canary tonight. Finalizer change: add explicit "unknown" bucket and avoid counting into reserved; update reconciliation pipeline and re-run for Feb to compute corrected invoice.
billing-bot: Created billing ticket BILL-8912: "Provisional credit request for pool-2234 due to reconciliation attribution bug". Current estimate: credit ~242 GPU-hours * $4/hr = $968.
Jordan B.: Please hold credit approval until finance signs off, but we can offer provisional credit and mark as pending. Maya, give ACME the provisional credit number and that we're investigating root cause + timeline for fix.
Sam C.: I'll coordinate the customer comms. Suggested message: "We're seeing an internal reconciliation issue that mis-attributed ~242 GPU hours to your reserved pool. We're preparing a provisional credit (~$968) while we fix the root cause and re-run reconciliation. We'll follow up with audit logs and timeline within 48 hours." Thoughts? :thumbsup: 
Maya S.: Good. Also include repro trace and high-level engineering explanation. Customer asked whether SLAs/credits will be impacted: answer — SLA unaffected, billing correction only.
Ashok R.: After we push fix and re-run finalizer, I'll attach the corrected CSV and the diff (before vs after). Running the corrected job now in a sandbox — I'll post results.
ops-oncall-bot: Canary rollout scheduled on infra-stage at 2026-03-01T02:00Z for route-agent v1.14.1.
Ashok R.: Sandbox finalizer run shows corrected_reserved_hours = 480, corrected_burst_hours = 360, corrected_total = 840 (matches raw total hours) — final invoiced reserved hours should be 480, so the 242 moves to burst.
Jordan B.: Finance approved provisional credit up to $1,000 pending audit. I'll update BILL-8912 and mark as approved-pending-audit.
Maya S.: I sent the initial message to the customer with the provisional credit and ETA for full reconciliation (48h). Customer replied: "Thanks, appreciate the quick triage. Please confirm when fixed."
Ashok R.: Creating PRs: route-agent fix (PR#482), finalizer patch (PR#483). Will request reviews.
Maya S.: Closing loop: once PRs merge and corrected invoice is posted, we will issue official credit and send a reconciliation report. Keeping this thread updated. :white_check_mark:
